newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney Olympics chief sees Stadium issue shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Sydney Olympics chief sees Stadium issue shortfall.

text.p: Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG) president Michael Knight said on Thursday that there was likely to be a shortfall for the public float of Stadium Australia.
Stadium Australia is seeking A$364.4 million to fund the construction of Sydney's Olympic stadium to host the 2000 Games.
"It is not a direct concern to either the government or to SOCOG, although obviously we would prefer that the Stadium float was better subscribed than is apparently the case," Knight told reporters.

Knight said he did not have any details on subscription levels to the float, which closes at 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT) today. Newspaper reports have put the Stadium shortfall at up to A$240 million, which would make it one of Australia's biggest share flops.
"It was a risk taken by the private sector fully, underwritten by the private sector and the large merchant banks have indicated...that they would meet any shortfall," he said.
The four underwriters are ANZ Securities, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Macquarie Bank Ltd and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
"If there is a shortfall, (and) that appears to be the case, after today they will still have a considerable period of time to trade their way out of trouble," Knight said.

"Today is not the drop-dead date for the underwriters, they have at least another 18 months to trade their way out of trouble," said Knight, who is also Olympics Minister for the New South Wales state government.
"The money is absolutely guaranteed, the stadium construction is rocketing ahead and will not be affected in any way by the difficulties the underwriters are facing in recouping the money," he said.
Stadium Australia opened its offer of 34,400 gold packages at A$10,000 each and 600 platinum passes at A$33,000 each on October 7 and had planned to close on November 29.

This was first extended to December 13 and has since been extended to close today. A spokeswoman for Stadium Australia told Reuters that it would not release the details of the float until at least late next week.
The gold packages include a seat at every stadium session of the 2000 Olympic Games, stadium membership for 30 years and 1,000 shares in the stadium company itself.
The platinum package include two priority seats and membership privileges.
